section_summary.extract_value: The section reports that, in a single study of female undergraduates, body appreciation, media influence (three SATAQ-3 subscales), and participant weight status significantly predicted consideration of cosmetic surgery, explaining 47.1% of variance; body appreciation was the strongest predictor. It notes unexpected findings (higher consideration among more slender participants and a negative correlation with age), discusses limitations (restricted undergraduate sample, limited variables), and recommends replication with representative community samples; the section does not label this as 'Study 1' or multiple studies.
section_summary.evidence_source: "The results of the current study showed that body appreciation... were significant predictors of consideration of cosmetic surgery among female undergraduates, explaining 47.1% of the variance." Additional supporting sentences include: "First, although participant BMI was a significant predictor... more slender participants reported greater consideration of cosmetic surgery." and "As such, these results may not be generalisable to other sample of women and it would be beneficial to replicate the current work using representative samples from the community."
